The binational La Amistad reservoir, the main water-supply source for Nuevo Laredo and Laredo, Texas, has recovered after more than three months at its lowest level of the year, El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo reported.

Storage rose from 19 percent of capacity in mid-July to 28 percent in the second half of October, a net gain of more than 350 million cubic meters. In absolute terms, storage climbed from 756 million cubic meters on July 14 to more than 1,114 million cubic meters by Oct. 19, the paper reported.

Ramón Meza González, head of the Mexican section of the Comisión Internacional de Límites y Aguas (CILA) in Nuevo Laredo, attributed part of the increase to recent rainfall in Coahuila, Chihuahua and Texas, according to the report. The Falcón reservoir also rose, from 14 percent to 16.7 percent of its useful capacity.

CILA said monitoring of the Rio Bravo would remain rigorous, and authorities urged residents on both sides of the border to use water efficiently and responsibly. Overall volumes remain below historical storage averages, even though the recovery supports water-treatment plant operations in the short and medium term, the paper reported.

Sources: El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, “Crece nivel de la presa La Amistad, principal fuente de abastecimiento de agua para los dos Laredos,” by Martha Martínez, Oct. 23, 2026.

title: La Amistad reservoir climbs to 28% capacity, a boost for both Laredos' water supply
